definition: Delta measures how much a portfolio's or option's value changes for a given change in the underlying's price; it is the first derivative of price with respect to the underlying.
core_idea: Delta is the most commonly used Greek, analogous to velocity in a car trip: just as velocity is the first derivative of distance with respect to time, delta is the first derivative of an option's value with respect to the underlying's price.
key_points: Delta can relate a portfolio's value to a broad benchmark (e.g., a stock portfolio to the S&P 500) or an option's value to its specific underlying.
The car-trip analogy: distance traveled relates to time similarly to how an option's value relates to the underlying price, with delta playing the role of velocity.
relationships: First derivative of price with respect to underlying
Gamma is the derivative of delta
trading_implications: Delta is the primary measure traders use to gauge directional exposure to the underlying.
